articles.title: An IIT Delhi graduate learned his family has a debt of Rs 1 crore while he was still a student; after building an app business and joining Google, Yash Garg cleared the debt in 2023 and started a new company
articles.summary: Yash Garg had planned to become an entrepreneur after graduating from IIT Delhi.
articles.body: Yash Garg had planned to become an entrepreneur after graduating from IIT Delhi. But during his second year at the institute, he discovered that his parents were dealing with more than ₹1 crore in debt. He put his startup plans on hold, decided to find a high-paying job and set himself a target: repay the loans so his parents could live without the financial pressure.Years later, he achieved that goal with help from a Google job and a mobile-app business he built with his father. The games they developed generated more than ₹2 crore in revenue over about 18 months. In June 2023, the family cleared its last loan. Garg then left Google to pursue the startup he had wanted to build since college.In a detailed post on X, Garg described how he discovered the debt and the decisions that followed. He studied at the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, graduating in 2019 with a BTech in Electrical Engineering and a minor in Computer Science.How he discovered his family's ₹1 crore debtGarg's father ran a real estate business and had invested in flats being built by developers. According to Garg, his father had paid a large part of the purchase price upfront through home loans. But the flats were not delivered for years, while the banks continued demanding monthly instalments.His parents began borrowing from friends and relatives to keep up with the payments. When that was not enough, they turned to credit cards. They did not tell their son the full extent of the financial trouble, hoping to protect him from the stress.That changed during his second year at IIT Delhi. Garg said collection agents began visiting the family home and asking for payments. He noticed how much the situation was affecting his mother and decided to find out exactly how much the family owed.He sat down with his parents and wrote down every outstanding amount, including loans from banks, friends, relatives and credit card companies. By the time he finished, the principal alone exceeded ₹1 crore. “I started from minus ₹1 crore, and I did not even know it until my second year at IIT Delhi,” he wrote on X.Until then, Garg had been focused on building a startup after college. The debt changed his immediate priorities. He decided to secure a well-paying job and repay the loans before returning to entrepreneurship.A failed placement attempt and a move to GoogleGarg initially aimed for a job at a high-frequency trading firm, where he hoped to earn more than ₹50 lakh a year. But his first day of campus placements did not go as planned. He eventually accepted an offer from Cohesity at ₹18 lakh a year. According to his X post, he moved to Bengaluru in July 2019, stayed in a paying guest accommodation, kept his monthly expenses below ₹20,000 and sent most of his earnings home.He later realised that his salary was not enough to clear the debt quickly. He began preparing for opportunities abroad and applied to Google and other companies in the US and UK in January 2020. However, the Covid-19 pandemic disrupted overseas hiring.As he explained in his X post, a senior from college who worked at Google advised him to consider a move that would help him repay the debt faster. The senior referred him to the company. Garg spent the next four months preparing for interviews, even after facing rejections from various companies. He eventually received an offer to join Google's Search team. He joined Google with an annual compensation package of around ₹75 lakh, including stock.How a ₹2.1 lakh laptop helped build a ₹2 crore businessWhen Garg joined Google, the family still had around ₹80 lakh in outstanding loans. He realised that his salary alone would take years to clear the amount. With Google's permission, he started developing mobile apps and games with his father, working on the business during nights and weekends.Their first Android apps did not generate revenue. Garg then compared the opportunities on Android and Apple's iOS platform and decided to try building games for iPhones.As he recounted on X, he bought a MacBook Pro for ₹2.1 lakh, selected their most-downloaded Android game and built its iOS version in six days. The game attracted downloads soon after its launch. Once they enabled monetisation, the earnings recovered the laptop's cost within a few days. The business then began growing. Garg said revenue increased from ₹6 lakh in the first month to ₹24 lakh in the fourth month as they added more games. Balancing his Google job and the app business meant working close to 100 hours a week, he said. The business generated more than ₹2 crore in revenue.The income from the games, along with his Google salary, finally allowed Garg and his parents to start reducing the principal instead of spending most of their money on interest. In his X post, he described paying off the loans one by one and seeing the stress at home gradually ease. In June 2023, they made the final payment. Garg resigned from Google soon after. He said his last working day was the day before his 25th birthday.From failed games to a funded AI startupLeaving Google did not mean that his entrepreneurial journey immediately became successful. Garg said he built 12 new games over the next four months, but none gained traction. He shut down the games business and moved into software-as-a-service (SaaS). His first attempt at building Shopify apps did not work out either. He then studied around 70 business-to-business SaaS marketplaces and decided to develop apps for users of monday, a project management platform.His first app for the platform also failed because it addressed a narrow need. For the next product, he studied feature requests and chose a problem that users had repeatedly asked the platform to solve. That decision brought his first paying customer in April 2024, eight months after he left Google. The business, Super Workday, now has more than 300 paying customers, mostly in the US, and is approaching $100,000 in annual recurring revenue, according to reports. Garg said he began launching a new app every month. He also said the business helped pay for his sister's wedding.What is Yash Garg doing now?Garg has moved on from that AI executive assistant venture and was building another startup in stealth mode. Garg has described his startup journey as still being at an early stage, with more challenges ahead. But after putting his original ambition on hold to repay his family's debt, he is now back to building companies.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
